Correcting upward is uncomfortable and it is far cheaper before a commitment is made on the overstated version than after.
questions.mindset: Give a number in the form it will be repeated in, because it will be repeated without you.

questions.stem: A revised method statement for work on a stadium roof was emailed to 240 site workers and subcontractor supervisors three weeks ago, changing the sequence for anchoring lifelines. Yesterday a scaffolding crew was found working to the old sequence. Their supervisor's response was that the email was sent to him and that he has it in his inbox. What should the project manager do?

options.text: Treat the instruction as undelivered: stop the affected work, brief the crews face to face, and record who has been briefed.
options.rationale: The evidence is that behaviour did not change, which is the only measure that counts for a method statement, and the 240 recipients are all now suspect rather than just this crew.

options.text: Reissue the method statement with a read receipt required.
options.rationale: It asks the failed channel to prove delivery, when a receipt records that a file was opened and says nothing about whether a crew changed how it rigs a lifeline.

options.text: Take the failure up with the subcontractor's management under the contract.
options.rationale: It allocates blame for a live safety exposure while crews elsewhere on the roof may still be working to the superseded sequence.

options.text: Add a check on the current method statement to the daily briefing sheet.
options.rationale: A sound control for tomorrow that does nothing today for the other recipients who may be in exactly the same position as this crew.

questions.explanation: Where a communication exists to change what people do, it is not complete until the change in behaviour has been confirmed at the place the work happens. Sending, receipting and even acknowledging are all measures of transmission, and a single instance of the old method in use is evidence that transmission was mistaken for delivery across the whole distribution. The correct reading of one non-compliant crew is that the population is unverified, not that one supervisor failed.
questions.mindset: For an instruction that must change what people do, delivery is proved at the workface, not in the outbox.

questions.stem: Your squad builds a shared leak reporting app funded jointly by eight water companies. Yesterday the largest partner's press office announced that from next month customers in areas with no mobile signal will be able to log a leak offline and have it sync automatically. Offline capture sits untouched on the backlog and the sync design is unresolved. Enquiries have started, one from a trade title, and the other seven partners were not consulted. What should the project manager do?

options.text: Get the facts and a proposed form of words to the partnership's agreed spokesperson today, including what the app will actually do next month.
options.rationale: Speed and mandate both matter, and the agreed route is the only one that produces a correction all eight operators can stand behind, rather than a second contradictory claim.

options.text: Post a correction from the squad's own channels immediately, since speed is what matters.
options.rationale: A visible contradiction between partners is a bigger story than the original error, and the squad has no mandate to speak on behalf of eight companies.

options.text: Ask the operator's press office to withdraw the announcement.
options.rationale: A withdrawal leaves every customer who read it with nothing in its place, and the request assumes an authority over another organisation's communications that you do not have.

options.text: Bring offline booking forward so that the announcement becomes true.
options.rationale: It lets an external statement reprioritise the backlog, teaching every partner that the fastest route to the top of the list is a press release rather than a conversation.

questions.explanation: Where several organisations speak about one product, the correction route matters as much as the correction, because an uncoordinated fix reads as a dispute and multiplies the audience for the original claim. The work is to supply accurate facts and usable wording quickly to whoever is entitled to speak, and separately to close the gap that allowed an unverified claim out. Letting the claim stand and letting it drive the plan are the two failures that look most like decisiveness.
questions.mindset: Correct a public error quickly, and correct it through the route the partnership agreed.

questions.stem: Your depot maintenance system serves a train operator's board, which reads on track against the contracted milestone dates, and your own executive, which reads it against an internal plan running six weeks earlier. You issue one report. The operator finds amber alarming and your executive finds green complacent, and an external assurance reviewer has now flagged the two readings as inconsistent reporting. What should the project manager do?

options.text: Publish one set of facts with both baselines named, and state the status against each explicitly.
options.rationale: It keeps a single source of truth while making the reason for two different readings visible, which is what removes the appearance of inconsistency.

options.text: Report against the contracted dates only, since that is the commitment that binds.
options.rationale: It hides the internal plan and with it the six weeks of warning time that plan exists to create, so problems surface only once they are contractual.

options.text: Issue two reports, each written for its own audience.
options.rationale: Two documents drift apart within a few cycles, and the reviewer has just told you that visible inconsistency is precisely what is being noticed.

options.text: Ask the two organisations to agree a single definition of on track before you report again.
options.rationale: It suspends reporting on a negotiation between two organisations, and the two baselines exist for good reasons that a single definition would flatten.

questions.explanation: A status is a comparison, so it carries no meaning until the reference point is declared, and two audiences can hold different reference points for entirely legitimate reasons. Where that is true, the inconsistency an assurance reviewer finds is almost never dishonesty; it is measurement that was never stated. Suppressing one reference point loses the warning time it was created to provide, and maintaining separate documents for separate audiences guarantees drift, since nobody reconciles two things that are never read side by side.
questions.mindset: Name the baseline whenever you give a status, because a status is meaningless without it.
